Fields are the LAST cycle number a given audit type was run, or null if never done / not yet backfilled. Update this file in the SAME cycle you run any of these audit types on an Actor -- add/replace the relevant field with the current cycle number and a one-line note. Keys: varied_test (plain filter-combo rotation), enum_audit (checked enum/vocabulary fields for structurally-dead values), unreachable_remedy (checked that a zero-row message's suggested fix is actually reachable), competitor_audit (compared price/features against the named competitor). Dates below are backfilled from cycles 797-814's own summaries (already read this session, not fresh archaeology) -- treat gaps (nulls) as real unknowns, not omissions. Key added cycle 824: count_audit (checked whether an upstream API's total-match count, when surfaced to buyers, is exhaustive rather than an estimate, and whether deep pages are actually reachable).

app-store-reviews-scraper.note: cycle 833: only one real schema enum, `sort` (mostRecent/mostHelpful/favorable/critical). Unlike every other Actor in the facet-diff rotation, Apple's iTunes RSS review feed (itunes.apple.com/<cc>/rss/customerreviews/id=<id>/sortBy=<X>/page=<N>/json) is directly reachable from this box (no proxy needed, unlike google-news-scraper) -- probed sortBy directly with 13 candidate values incl. the 2 real ones plus 11 plausible-but-unlisted guesses (mostFavorable, mostCritical, topRated, newest, oldest, recent, helpful, rating, relevance, popular, trending). Only mostRecent/mostHelpful (the code's actual 2 API values) returned real entries (50 each); every other candidate returned HTTP 200 with an empty feed (no `entry` key at all) or HTTP 500 -- confirmed by inspecting the raw JSON body, not just entry count. favorable/critical are already correctly documented as client-side re-sorts of mostRecent, not real API params, so the 4-value schema enum is exhaustive and accurate. Clean audit, no code change. NOTE: cycle 832's queue note calling this 'the last enum_audit: null Actor' was wrong -- a fresh count after this cycle shows 12 Actors still null (ats-jobs, eu-ted-tenders, google-play-reviews, nih-reporter, remote-jobs, sam-gov-opportunities, sec-insider-trades, shopify-products, steam-reviews, substack, trademark-search, uk-find-a-tender). The rotation is not done; see queue.md. cycle 845: cycle 843/844 generalization applied here (watch baseline diffed against its own row shape). Apple keeps a review id stable when its author edits their own star rating (feed comment verified live 2026-09-26: a raw RSS entry has only author/rating/title/content/version/votes -- no developer-response field at all, unlike Google Play, so scoreChanged is the only applicable event here, not developerReplied/replyRemoved). Watch baseline was seenIds only -- no rating snapshot -- so an edited review was silently indistinguishable from an unedited one forever. Shipped watchEvents ([new, scoreChanged], empty = both) + watchEvent/previousScore output fields, backed by a seenMeta array (rating 1-5, 0 = pre-845 unknown, never fires) parallel to seenIds. Verified via 5 local round-trip scenarios against real live Apple review data (patching the LOCAL watch KV record, same technique as production KV patches in cycles 843/844, just local so nothing needed cleanup): (1) patched baseline rating differs from live rating + scoreChanged in watchEvents -> fires correctly with correct previousScore, exactly 1 of 20 pushed; (2) same patch + watchEvents:[new] (scoreChanged excluded) -> correctly silent, watchEventsFiltered counted, meta still updated to the live value so it cannot re-fire later; (3) meta silently re-synced after a fire -> third run byte-idempotent (0 pushed); (4) seenMeta key deleted entirely (pre-845 record simulation) -> zero false events, correct predates-change-detection log line; (5) a genuinely-absent id -> delivered as watchEvent:new, previousScore:null. Non-watch default-input regression byte-identical locally AND live on the platform (build 0.1.63, 5/5 charged). check-fail-ordering allowlist line numbers re-verified and updated (907/1146/1162, shifted from 815/1054/1070 by this change -- same 3 guard conditions read live in source, still safe). check-registry-fields/check-code-fields/check-readme-samples all clean after adding watchEvent/previousScore to registry.json output_fields + dataset_schema.json + README (input table, Watch mode section, Use cases bullet, new FAQ entry).
app-store-reviews-scraper.unreachable_remedy_note: cycle 1314: audited the pushed===0 zero-row branch (src/main.js ~1308-1316) covering 4 remedy paths. Live-verified the two with concrete, falsifiable remedies: (1) depthCappedPairs ("raise maxReviewsPerApp to search deeper") -- fetched Instagram/us mostRecent pages 1-3 live (50 entries each), rating=2 reviews appear on EVERY page (2+2+2), confirming a buyer capped at one page (maxReviewsPerApp=50) who filters to rating:2 really would recover more matches by raising the cap, since scanCap directly bounds scrapeAppCountrySort's page loop (line 749) and the cap is correctly distinguished from feedCeiling (Apple's own 500-review limit, where the code already avoids this remedy). (2) storefrontError 400/404 hint (getJson, line 463-467: "storefront code was X, two-letter ISO-3166-1 alpha-2, UK is gb not uk") -- live-reproduced the EXACT typo the hint names: GET itunes.apple.com/uk/rss/... really does return HTTP 400 (confirmed live), so the hint fires on the real-world mistake it claims to catch, not a strawman. Also spot-checked the emptyPairs remedy (probeStorefronts, PROBE_COUNTRIES=us/gb/ca/au/de, 2 sorts x 2 pages x 2 client classes per country) structurally -- mechanism consistent with the same working RSS calls proven live in (1), not independently reproduced with a true region-locked positive case for lack of a confirmed region-locked app id. filteredOutPairs has no raise-X remedy to test (its text is just diagnostic: filters removed every scanned review). Genuinely clean -- no code/README change.
app-store-reviews-scraper.varied_test_note: cycle 1089: GROWTH slot, fleet-oldest varied_test (1037). FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BILLABLE BUG, not just a clean negative. Combo: multi-country array with an explicit country PLUS a second country whose countryFallback probe lands on that same explicit country -- countries:["bt","us"] + countryFallback:true (Bhutan, id bt, genuinely has 0 reviews for Notion id1232780281, verified free via direct itunes.apple.com RSS probe before spending anything; its fallback probe order PROBE_COUNTRIES=[us,gb,ca,au,de] hits 'us' first, which the SAME run already also scrapes directly). Root cause: `seen` (per-reviewId dedup Set) was created fresh inside scrapeAppCountry() per (appId,country) pair, so nothing prevented the identical review (same reviewId) from being pushed and CHARGED twice -- once under the bt/fallback pair, once under the direct us pair -- live-reproduced pre-fix: 16 rows requested, 8 unique reviewIds each appearing exactly twice, byte-identical content both times. Not disclosed anywhere in the README. Fix (build 0.1.70, source 0.1.10->0.1.11): hoisted a `crossCountrySeen` Set to once-per-appId scope (outer apps-loop, before the countries loop) and threaded it into both scrapeAppCountry() call sites (direct + the countryFallback retry) instead of each call creating its own; reviewId namespace is globally unique per Apple review so cross-country dedup can never conflate two genuinely different reviews. Verified live post-fix on the exact repro input: 14/14 unique reviewIds, 0 duplicates, bt-fallback rows correctly tagged (requestedCountry:bt, fallbackUsed:true) then us-direct rows correctly continue with NEW reviews beyond what bt's fallback already delivered (no re-fetch-and-skip waste). Negative-control regression: default test_input.json (single country, no fallback triggered) unchanged, 10/10 unique. README FAQ entry added (v0.1.11) disclosing the fix. Build 0.1.71 (README) verified live via the build's readme field. All standing checks clean after (check-pricing 24/29/0, check-charges 24/24, check-competitor-claims 62/0 + 40/0).

Live-reproduced on id1434243584 (Lex Fridman, 500+ episodes) with minReleaseDate/maxReleaseDate=2019-01: log showed '100 episodes fetched, 0 kept after filters' yet the buyer-facing status message flatly denied a valid podcast ID was ever parsed -- actively wrong, not just silent, for a namable and common case (any date/duration/explicit filter set outside Apple's ~200-most-recent-episode window on the non-RSS path). Fixed (build 0.1.51): scrapeEpisodes() now also returns whether it used the RSS wholeFeed path; the per-id loop detects got>0 && kept===0 && !wholeFeed && filters-set and records the id in a new `windowFilteredIds` list with its own log.warning naming the cap and pointing at useRssForFullArchive; wired into both the pushed===0 'why' chain (ahead of the generic fallback) and a new pushed>0 branch (parallel to depthCapped) for the partial-fleet case. Live-verified 2 ways post-push: (1) same repro input -> statusMessage now correctly reads 'Apple's lookup API only returned each show's recent episode window for: 1434243584, and your minReleaseDate (2019-01-01) / maxReleaseDate (2019-01-31) filter(s) removed all of them -- turn on \"useRssForFullArchive\" to search the full archive instead.'; (2) default-input regression gate SUCCEEDED, chargedEventCounts {result: 46}, statusMessage None (unaffected). check-fail-ordering flagged the known-safe h289 seed gate at its shifted line (1069->1096, ~27 net lines added above it by this fix) -- re-verified the guard condition is byte-identical, allowlist updated, back to 0 suspects. check-pricing 0 drift/29, check-charges 24/24, check-code-fields/check-registry-fields/check-readme-samples all 0 drift, 3 services active, /health + /tools/apple-podcasts-scraper both 200. | cycle 893: FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BUG affecting a fleet-wide pattern, not just this Actor. input_schema.json podcasts field carried BOTH default and prefill = the Lex Fridman Podcast URL. Apify merges an input_schema default into ANY run (API/CLI/scheduler) that omits the field entirely -- so a buyer calling with only searchTerms set (the documented "find shows by keyword instead of ... giving URLs" path) silently ALSO got Lex Fridman Podcast episodes mixed into results with no warning, sharing the maxResults budget and starving the actual request (live-verified: searchTerms:["Darknet Diaries"], maxResults=6 returned 3 Lex Fridman rows + 3 real Darknet Diaries rows before the fix). Root cause: Apify distinguishes prefill (UI-only, never sent on omission) from default (merged into every run missing the field, including API calls) -- confirmed via Apify docs. Fix: removed the default key from podcasts in .actor/input_schema.json, kept prefill (Console one-click run UX unaffected). Live-verified post-push (build 0.1.48): searchTerms-only run now returns 6/6 genuine Darknet Diaries rows, 0 Lex Fridman; explicit podcasts input unchanged/still works; fully-empty input now fails cleanly via the Actor's own "provide at least one" validation instead of silently running Lex Fridman. Same default/prefill shape found and fixed in the SAME cycle on google-news-scraper (queries) and steam-reviews-scraper (apps) -- see their own varied_test notes. Not yet checked: app-store-reviews-scraper (apps/appNames) and google-play-reviews-scraper (appIds/searchTerms) have the same field shape and were NOT tested this cycle -- flagged in queue.md for the next QUALITY slot. | cycle 935: varied_test combo never exercised before -- watchLabel (episodes watch mode) crossed with MULTIPLE raw-RSS-only podcasts (no Apple id) in the same podcasts[] input. Found and FIXED a real cross-show identity collision: pushEpisodeRows() built watchId as `${row.collectionId ?? 'feed'}:${episodeId||episodeGuid||title}` -- every RSS-only show (collectionId always null for them, since scrapeEpisodesFromFeed passes null) fell back to the SAME literal string 'feed', not a per-show key, even though the adjacent floorKey/pairFloors logic already correctly disambiguates shows via `feed:${feedUrl}`. Reproduced live end-to-end with two synthetic local RSS feeds sharing an episode guid ("ep1", a realistic collision for cheap/DIY feed generators that guid by sequential per-show number): baseline over both feeds recorded only 1 seenIds entry instead of 2, and a later genuinely-new episode published on the second show (own distinct title/date, but happened to reuse guid "ep1") was silently reported as already-delivered -- 0 pushed, 0 charged, no warning, permanently invisible under that watch label. Fixed by falling back to the already-unique `floorKey` (not the literal 'feed') in the watchId formula -- zero behavior change for the Apple-ID path, where collectionId is always set and the fallback never triggers. Verified 3 ways + live: (1) local baseline with the fix now correctly records 2 distinct seenIds (`feed:<url1>:ep1`, `feed:<url2>:ep1`); (2) the same later-new-episode scenario is now correctly delivered (1 pushed) once its guid is genuinely its own; (3) Apple-ID watch regression byte-identical (5/5 seenIds unchanged, same `<collectionId>:<episodeId>` shape). Live on the platform (build 0.1.50): default-input gate SUCCEEDED 5/5 charged; a real single-feed raw-RSS watch baseline (feeds.simplecast.com) persisted seenIds as `feed:<feedUrl>:<guid>` in the shared production KV store, confirmed via the API, then the test record was deleted.
apple-podcasts-scraper.watch_subset_note: cycle 853: CLEAN NEGATIVE, formally recorded. Cycle 852 guessed this Actor would be the fleet's next counter-field case (rating/review counts, like hacker-news-scraper) -- wrong guess, because watchLabel is explicitly restricted to dataType="episodes" only (src/main.js:103-112); review counts/ratings live under dataType="reviews"/"podcasts", which have no watch mode at all, so the counter-mutation risk never reaches watch-mode code. Checked the episodes watch path itself instead: baseline is a bare id Set (watchId = collectionId:episodeId|episodeGuid|title, main.js:610), no snapshot of any field. But the README (line 40, "Watch mode" section) promises ONLY new-episode detection ("only episodes not delivered under that label before") -- unlike every other watch-mode Actor in the fleet (Shopify/Play/App Store/Steam/ATS/court-records/HN), it never promises a field-change alert on an already-delivered id, so the watch-subset-shape defect (a promised field-change silently missed because the baseline is narrower than the row) cannot apply here by definition -- there is no promised change signal to miss. Checked the plausible mutation candidates anyway (explicit-tag correction, duration correction, releaseDate correction under a stable episodeId) and confirmed episodePassesFilters() runs BEFORE the watchSeen check (main.js:607-616), so an episode that initially fails a filter (e.g. explicitFilter=clean excluding a mistagged-explicit episode) is never added to the baseline and self-heals if corrected later -- same accidental-coverage shape Play had (cycle 844). No code change.

Closed queue item 0-TODO-h855-pagination. ROOT CAUSE, reproduced live before touching code: Postgres sorts NULLs FIRST on a DESC sort, and schedule_a/schedule_b were queried with sort=-contribution_receipt_date / -disbursement_date and NO sort_nulls_last (schedule_e has always had sort_nulls_last:'true' -- A and B were the odd ones out). A real minority of Schedule A/B rows have a NULL date (F3X filers leave the itemization date blank), so any match set containing one starts with a block of dateless rows, and inside that block FEC's keyset cursor is {last_index, sort_null_only:true} with NO last_<date> value. The code explicitly stripped sort_null_only from the cursor ('a flag, not a cursor value'), so page 2 carried last_index alone -> HTTP 422 'both values from the previous page's last_indexes object are needed'. Verified: unfiltered 2026 schedule_a page 1 = 100 rows, ALL dates null, li={last_index, sort_null_only:true}; replaying page 2 with last_index only = 422 (the exact cycle-855 error), with sort_null_only=true = 200. KEY FINDING -- forwarding sort_null_only ALONE IS NOT A FIX, it converts a loud failure into SILENT TRUNCATION: on a deliberately mixed 2-committee match set (C00406892 = 320 dateless rows, C00002469 = 13,693 dated rows) the sort_null_only walk delivered all 320 dateless rows then returned last_indexes={} at page 5 -- i.e. 'exhausted' -- never reaching ANY of the 13,693 dated rows. A PPE buyer would be charged for 320 useless rows and told that was the whole result set. FIX = both halves: (1) primary -- sort_nulls_last:'true' added to schedule_a and schedule_b (parity with schedule_e), so dateless rows go to the TAIL and the useful walk always carries a real date cursor; (2) defensive -- stop stripping sort_null_only (normalised to the string 'true', false/null dropped) so the trailing null block pages instead of 422ing. VERIFIED on platform build 0.1.31: same mixed-set walk with sort_nulls_last started at the newest dated rows and paged 8+ pages on a proper date cursor; a real filtered run (donorEmployer BOEING, electionYear 2026, maxResults 45) SUCCEEDED across 3 pages -- 45 rows, 0 nulls, dates verified strictly descending 2026-08-31 -> 2026-08-27, so the page-2/3 cursors genuinely work; default-input gate (candidateName Warren) SUCCEEDED, 3 results, no regression. All 8 standing checks clean, 0 drift. NEW BEHAVIOUR / NOT A REGRESSION BUT WORTH KNOWING: sort_nulls_last makes the fully UNFILTERED contributions scan (electionYear only, ~173M matching rows) too expensive upstream -- it 504s on curl and now times out fecGet's 30s request budget on page 1, so that one shape fails with 0 rows charged instead of failing with 100 dateless rows charged. Judged net-positive and shipped; the unactionable timeout message is queued as 0-TODO-h856-unfiltered. The trailing-null-block transition (half 2) is defensive and NOT live-verified -- reaching it needs all dated rows exhausted first (137+ pages on the smallest mixed set found), so it was out of budget to prove.

FOUND AND FIXED A REAL TIMEZONE BUG (same shape as cycle 996's Apple storefront-offset bug, different source). Every Federal Register date is an EASTERN calendar date (issue live 8:45am ET, comment period closes 11:59pm ET on comments_close_on), but the code derived 'today' via isoDay() = toISOString() = UTC. Actor runs execute in UTC, 4-5h AHEAD of ET, so for any run between 00:00-04:00 UTC (05:00 in EST) conditions[comment_date][gte] was set to the NEXT Eastern day and dropped every document closing on the current ET day -- exactly the most urgent rows, the ones the schema promises as 'the deadline set a buyer still has time to act on'. DST-correct: cutover at 04:00 UTC in EDT, 05:00 UTC in EST, verified on 6 instants. Build 0.1.28, package 0.1.3 -> 0.1.4. NOT fixable by widening the walk ourselves: `archived` is hundreds of thousands of rows and enriching them would blow the time budget while delivering opportunities the buyer never asked for. Both cycle-895-tied candidates (sec-insider-trades-scraper, substack-scraper) had already gotten thorough multi-combo coverage AT cycle 895 itself (verified by reading their own notes) so moved to the next-oldest untested candidate, shopify-products-scraper (901). Live-tested an angle not covered by cycle 901s filter-combo pass or cycle 843s onSale-watch-event work: watch-mode maxProductsPerStore cap enforcement. FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BUG: the schema promises the cap "caps how many products are SCANNED per store" in watch mode, but main.js only checked the cap at page boundaries (scanCapped() in the outer for-loop condition) -- since Shopify pages are always up to 250 products, ANY maxProductsPerStore below 250 was silently ignored for the first page: set to 40, live run logged "stopped after scanning 250 products (maxProductsPerStore = 40)" (reproduced twice: 40 and 10, both scanned exactly 250). Fixed (build 0.1.63) by moving the cap check inside the per-product loop (mirroring non-watch modes existing got>=perStore break), with a capBroke flag so a mid-page cap break is never mistaken for sweptToEnd (which would have caused FALSE delisted verdicts on real products just past the cap -- caught and fixed before shipping, not after). Verified live post-fix: maxProductsPerStore=40 now logs "stopped after scanning 40 products" exactly. Default-input regression (10 rows, non-watch) unaffected. Test watch records (qtest941cap, qtest941cap2) deleted from the shared production KV store after verification. check-pricing/check-code-fields/check-fail-ordering all clean post-fix. | cycle 992 varied_test: targeted detailLevel:"full" — the paid enrichment path, never exercised under the QUALITY rotation (cycle 843 had dismissed it as "our own internal fetch-depth switch, nothing to audit" as an ENUM, which is true, but the code path itself had never been live-tested). Clean on the enrichment itself: full-detail run landed seoTitle/ratingValue/reviewCount/hasSubscriptionOption/totalInventory; totalInventory lands even with includeVariants:false (confirming main.js:616's comment claim); productDetail charges matched delivered rows 1:1 (3 rows -> result:3/productDetail:3), so the "filtered-out products are never charged" promise holds on the PAID path too. Also verified availableOf()'s inventory-quantity fallback id-for-id across all THREE Shopify routes (bulk /products.json, single /products/<h>.json, /products/<h>.js) on a part-sold-out allbirds product: all 7 variants agreed exactly, 1 of 7 available — the single-product route does carry inventory_quantity, so availabilityUnknown/null is rarer than the code comments imply. FOUND AND FIXED A REAL RUN-KILLING BUG (build 0.1.65), reproduced live by accident during the above: currencyFor() fetched the OPTIONAL /meta.json (supplies nothing but the `currency` field, already null-on-any-failure) through http()'s FULL retry ladder — 3 outer attempts x 40s, run twice over by http()'s accept-language fallback. It is the FIRST call of the store loop, so request()'s per-call clamp to "budget actually left" is the whole run and does not help. A transient Apify Proxy UPSTREAM502 on allbirds.com/meta.json consumed the ENTIRE 240s run before a single product was fetched: run TIMED-OUT, 0 rows, 0 charged events — a flaky optional metadata endpoint zeroing out a paid catalog scrape. Survived the c712-c715 per-request-clamp sweep because that fix bounds each call to the remaining budget rather than asking whether the call is load-bearing at all. FIXED with the Actor's own existing idiom (the empty-page re-check's "a nicety, not the result"): single gotScraping attempt, retry.limit 0, hard 8s cap (CURRENCY_MAX_MS), skipped outright when remainingMs() <= cap + MIN_REQUEST_MS, and every failure/skip now logs a warning explaining the null instead of leaving it unexplained; dataset_schema `currency` given a description saying the same. VERIFIED LIVE ON THE SAME ENDPOINT THAT BROKE IT: identical input, before = TIMED-OUT/0 rows/0 charges; after = failed in exactly 8000ms with the new warning, run SUCCEEDED in 29s, 3 rows, currency null-and-explained, charges 3/3. CF's own feed structurally never emits those two tags -- the cycle-838 note's "all with real non-trivial data" claim was WRONG (it likely only checked that the param didn't 400 and that rows came back, not that the returned tag matched the requested stage). Since matches() trusts the real release tag, CF can NEVER contribute a contract/implementation row, no matter sources/stages. FIXED (build 0.1.38): added a CF_BLIND_STAGES startup warning (fires whenever stages includes contract/implementation and sources includes cf, explaining CF cannot match and what to do), a new RUN_SUMMARY.cfBlindStagesRequested field, corrected the false cycle-838-derived code comment above FTS_STAGES, and corrected the README FAQ's "Contracts Finder's own filter already handles all 5 values correctly" claim. FOUND A REAL BUG. matches() matched searchQuery words and keywordsAny phrases with a bare hay.includes(), i.e. MID-WORD substring. Live proof on a 14-day window: the README's own flagship example searchQuery='IT support' returned 'Supply of Specialist Military Clothing' (mil-IT-ary), 'Kier Infrastructure - UXO Site Surveys' (s-IT-e), 'CA18502 - Architectural Services' (arch-IT-ectural) in its top 10; decisive control searchQuery='ilitar lothing' (two pure mid-word fragments that are not words at all) returned 'Supply of Specialist Military Clothing' - substring matching confirmed, not inferred. Users were charged $0.003/result for rows containing the search word nowhere. FIXED (build 0.1.43): added atWordStart(hay,needle) - indexOf loop asserting the char before the hit is not [\p{L}\p{N}] (no lookbehind regex, no escaping), applied to BOTH searchWords.every and keywordsAny.some. Deliberately a word-START anchor, not a full word-boundary: keeps the useful half of substring search (stem/prefix - 'consult'->'consultancy', 'support'->'supporting') while killing mid-word collisions. Needles opening with a non-word char ('-19','&co') fall back to plain includes() so they stay findable. 14-case local unit check passed (incl. 'ware' NOT matching 'software', '19' matching 'covid-19', 'it' matching '(it) helpdesk' but not 'military'/'site'/'architectural').
